:::{#thm-loocv-shortcut}
#### Leave-one-out cross-validation for least squares

For a linear model fitted by [ordinary least squares](correlation-regression.qmd#def-ols)
with every [leverage](#def-leverage) $\lev{\iobs} < 1$,
the [leave-one-out estimate](#def-loocv)
can be computed from the single fit to all $\nobs$ observations,
from its [fitted values](prediction.qmd#def-fitted-value) $\fitted_{\iobs}$,
their [prediction errors](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error)
$\prederr_{\iobs} = \fitted_{\iobs} - \outvar_{\iobs}$,
and the leverages:

$$
\cvest{\nobs} = \frac{1}{\nobs} \sum_{\iobs \in \obsidx} \sqf{\frac{\prederr_{\iobs}}{1 - \lev{\iobs}}}.
$$ {#eq-loocv-shortcut}

:::

::: proof
Not derived here;
see the sources named under the theorem.
The derivation needs a formula for how the inverse of the
[cross-product matrix](#def-cross-product-matrix) $\sscp$
changes when one observation's outer product $\soprod{\termvec{\iobs}}$ is removed from it
(the Sherman--Morrison formula),
which this page does not develop.
:::

:::{#rem-source-loocv-shortcut}
#### Source: Leave-one-out cross-validation for least squares

@james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.2] states this formula for least squares linear or polynomial regression,
and @hastie2009elements [sec. 7.10.1] for many linear fitting methods.

:::
